newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Russia's Lebed brings plan to former "lion's den".
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed brings plan to former "lion's den".

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed entered what for two decades of his army career was the enemy "Lion's Den" on Monday, promising proposals to defuse a dispute between NATO and Russia over alliance expansion plans.

Former paratroop general Lebed, on his first visit to the West, was met at NATO headquarters by Secretary-General Javier Solana. Wearing a crisp, black suit he smiled and shrugged his shoulders at a barrage of media questions.
The headquarters, a rambling fenced complex of low brick buildings, was the object of particular scorn in Cold War Soviet literature, described variously as a "nest of vipers" and the "Lion's Den".

This post-Cold War meeting will give Western officials a chance to sound out President Boris Yeltsin's security adviser who, while the foreign ministry has eased its opposition, has remained fiercely critical of alliance plans to absorb former Kremlin Warsaw Pact allies such as Poland.
The 46-year-old former paratroop commander and Afghan war veteran said on arrival in Brussels on Sunday he had proposals to tackle the dispute, but he gave no details.

He gave a hint, however, that he would have some blunt words for the NATO alliance, which he once described as behaving like a "drunken hooligan" over the expansion plan. He said he expected a "complicated but civilised dialogue".
He says NATO has not adapted enough to the new era in Europe.

Lebed was appointed chief security adviser by Yeltsin on the strength of his performance in the first round of presidential elections this summer. But he has met strong opposition in the government and administration over his tough, independent style.

Tipped by opinion pollsters as a favourite to succeed Yeltsin, who undergoes heart surgery later this year, Lebed has stirred intense interest among officials and news media alike in the NATO headquarters city.
